title: Exact Trotterization in the Degenerate Quantum Rabi Model
abstract: Digital quantum simulation of the quantum Rabi model in the deep strong coupling regime motivates the need for an exact characterization of Trotterization errors, so far known only through qualitative bounds. Here we derive such a characterization in the exactly solvable degenerate limit, valid for arbitrary coupling strength. The first-order Trotter operator admits a closed expression, showing that the generated phase-space trajectory lies exactly on a circle that is rescaled and rigidly rotated with respect to the exact one, rather than merely approximating it. This geometric renormalization yields a closed form for the state fidelity, structurally identical to the physical survival probability governing revivals in the deep strong coupling regime: both are the same geometric question -- the distinguishability of a displaced Fock state -- applied to two different pairs of points in phase space. We further show that this geometric error is exactly correctable by promoting the Trotter-step coupling to a complex amplitude, at no additional circuit cost. These results, obtained in the exactly solvable degenerate limit, provide a benchmark for Trotterization errors in the general Rabi model.
summary: This theoretical paper provides an exact characterization of Trotterization errors for simulating the Quantum Rabi Model in the deep strong coupling regime. By analyzing the degenerate limit, the authors show the error manifests as a predictable geometric renormalization of the phase-space trajectory. Crucially, they derive a method to exactly cancel this error by modifying the Trotter-step coupling to a complex amplitude.
main_problem: The paper addresses the need for an exact characterization of Trotterization errors when digitally simulating the Quantum Rabi Model (QRM) in the deep strong coupling regime.
main_result: The first-order Trotter operator generates a phase-space trajectory that is exactly a rescaled and rotated version of the true path, and this geometric error is exactly correctable by modifying the Trotter-step coupling to a complex amplitude.
method: The authors derived closed-form expressions for the first-order Trotter operator and analyzed the resulting state fidelity by mapping the error to a geometric renormalization problem in phase space.
model_or_system: The system is the Quantum Rabi Model (QRM), describing the interaction between a two-level system (qubit) and a bosonic mode. The analysis is performed in the exactly solvable degenerate limit ($\omega_0 = 0$), simplifying the Hamiltonian to $H = \omega a^\dagger a + g \sigma_x(a + a^\dagger)$.
key_observables: State fidelity ($F(t)$), survival probability ($S(t)$), and the phase-space trajectory of the bosonic annihilation operator $\langle a(t) angle$.
important_parameters: Deep Strong Coupling (DSC) regime ($g \gtrsim \omega \gg \omega_0$), the coupling strength $g$, and the time step $\delta t$.
main_assumptions:
The derived closed-form results are strictly limited to the degenerate limit ($\omega_0 = 0$); extension to $\omega_0 
eq 0$ requires numerical methods.
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows the revival probability $S(t)$ vs. time for the degenerate limit. Figure 2 compares exact vs. Trotterized phase-space trajectories. Figure 3 compares exact, Trotterized, and renormalized phase-space evolution. Figure 4 shows the fidelity $F$ vs. time, demonstrating exact revivals.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical problem in the DSC regime, derives the closed-form error characterization in the degenerate limit, shows the geometric renormalization of the error, and finally proposes an exact, cost-free correction mechanism.
why_interesting: This work provides a deep, geometric understanding of systematic errors in quantum simulation, showing that the error structure itself is governed by the same underlying physics (displaced Fock state distinguishability) as the physical phenomena being simulated.

FIG. 3. Phase-space trajectories of ⟨a(t)⟩for the exact evolu- tion (blue circle), the first-order Trotterized simulation with 7 steps (red polygon), and the continuously evolved renormal- ized model with coupling eλ and phase −θ/2 (black circle). The polygon vertices fall exactly on the black circle, confirm- ing that the Trotterized dynamics reproduces the renormal- ized model exactly. Crosses mark the exact and effective circle centers, −λ and −eλe−iθ/2, the latter rotated by −θ/2 relative to the former, as indicated by the arc. Parameters: λ = 2, initial state |+, 0⟩.
